question: Through which Amendment of the Indian Constitution was the Right to Education designated as a Fundamental Right?
solution:
The correct answer is __**86th Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **86th Amendment Act**, enacted in 2002, inserted **Article 21A** into the Indian Constitution, making the Right to Education a Fundamental Right.
 
• It mandates that the State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children aged **6 to 14 years**.
 
• To operationalize this, the **Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act (RTE Act)** was passed in 2009 and came into effect on April 1, 2010.
 
• The amendment also modified **Article 45**, obligating the State to provide early childhood care and education to children below six years of age.
 
• Additionally, it inserted **Article 51A(k)**, specifying that parents or guardians must provide opportunities for education to their children aged 6 to 14 years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights**:

 
 
• Fundamental Rights are enshrined in **Part III** of the Indian Constitution, ensuring basic rights to all citizens.
 
• They are enforceable by the courts and protect citizens from arbitrary actions by the State.
 
• Articles 12 to 35 cover various Fundamental Rights, including the right to equality, freedom, and education.
 
 
 
• **Article 21A**:
 
 
• Introduced by the 86th Amendment, Article 21A provides the Right to Education as a Fundamental Right.
 
• This article ensures that every child aged 6 to 14 years has access to free and compulsory education.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009**:
 
 
• The RTE Act is a legislative framework to implement the provisions of Article 21A.
 
• It specifies the responsibilities of the central and state governments, schools, and parents in ensuring universal education.
 
• It also mandates a 25% reservation for economically weaker sections in private schools.
 
 
 
• **Early Childhood Care and Education**:
 
 
• Article 45, as amended, emphasizes the importance of pre-primary education for children below six years of age.
 
• Programs like **Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS)** aim to cater to this need.
